messages:
alex_m: FYI we got a returned ACH from Sable Corp (acct ending ··4321). Bank returned: "invalid destination bank code". Customer says they used the routing number we accepted via API earlier today.
priya_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the raw payload we sent to the bank (redact acct)?
alex_m: Sent to #private-ticket: payload looked like: ```{
  "beneficiary_name": "Sable Corp",
  "account_number": "****4321",
  "routing_number": "012345678",  // coming from customer
  "currency": "USD"
}``` but our wire translation logs show we forwarded routing as "12345678" (leading zero missing).
priya_support: ah that mismatch would cause the bank to reject. Did any transform run on the field?
payments-bot: [auto] Payment ID pay_987654 queued -> forwarded to ACH gateway -> gateway rejected code 402 (invalid routing).
max_payops: Checking gateway logs now — we see our gateway piece logs: `routing=12345678` (no leading zero). Upstream payload in our ingestion service contained `"routing_number": "012345678"`. Looks like normalization stripped leading zero.
erin_engineering: That sounds like integer coercion in the JSON schema. I ran a quick grep: payments-ingest parses routing_number with `Integer.parseInt()` for legacy checks. We should treat routing_number as string.
priya_support: Customer is upset, they want resubmit + refund of fees. Sable POC is Jenna (jenna@sable.example). They need an ETA.
alex_m: Created INC-4821 and added all logs + gateway rejection. Can we do a hotfix to stop integer coercion? Also add pre-send validation to catch length/leading zero.
erin_engineering: I'll open PR to change the parser to keep as string and add a validation rule: routing_number must match `^0?\d{8,9}$` and preserve leading zeros. Also will add unit test for `012345678` -> stays `012345678`.
max_payops: Can we patch gateway adapter to reject if length != 9 and to emit the bank's error code in our logs? That would make root-cause quicker.
priya_support: For immediate customer relief: I offered to resubmit after we confirm the corrected payload. Sable approved if we can resubmit within 2h. Also asked for a credit for return fees.
erin_engineering: Timeline: I'll have a patch branch by EOD, hotfix to prod if tests pass (estimated +3h). We should coordinate a config toggle to enable stricter validation behind a flag.
max_payops: I'll queue a manual resubmit once engineering confirms payload formatting. Also will process fee credit after incident closed.
alex_m: Note to ops: when resubmitting, include `bank_note: original_return_reason=invalid_destination_bank_code` so downstream reconcilers track this.
priya_support: Thanks. I'll keep customer updated. Assigning follow-ups: @erin_engineering patch parser + tests, @max_payops manual resubmit + fee credit, @alex_m add e2e test that checks routing preservation.
alex_m: tl;dr root cause = routing_number got coerced to integer -> dropped leading zero -> bank rejected. Fix = treat as string + add validation and logging.
payments-bot: [auto] INC-4821 updated: status -> investigating; assignees: erin_engineering,max_payops,alex_m.
priya_support: Recording resolution steps here so we can close the escalation after resubmit: 1) Patch ingest to keep routing_number as string. 2) Add pre-send validation for length and leading zeros. 3) Add explicit mapping that doesn't trim leading zeros. 4) Resubmit payment and handle customer fee credit.
max_payops: Done — manual resubmit succeeded at 1952301290, bank accepted on retry. Marking this returned issue as resolved on our side; waiting on refunds flow.
alex_m: thanks team. Closing thread once refund done. :white_check_mark:
